$comment: Claude Code hook configuration for the agentic-auto-improve plugin.
Referenced from .claude-plugin/plugin.json as "hooks". It deliberately lives
beside the hooks rather than at the plugin root, because _project_paths.py
resolves its search root as Path(__file__).parent.parent -- that is, the
'.claude' directory two levels up from a hook file. Moving the hooks to a
root-level hooks/ directory would resolve SELF_ROOT to the repository root
and every registry, area-map and contract lookup would silently miss.
THE PLUGIN IS THE SOURCE OF ITS HOOKS. A project that installs this plugin
registers none of these hooks itself. Registering one again makes it run twice,
because Claude Code does not merge a project hook with the same command in a
plugin's hooks.json: both run.
EXEC FORM: every entry names the interpreter as "command": "py" and the
arguments as "args": ["-3", "<script>", ...]. No shell parses the line, so a
path with a space needs no quoting. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} always resolves to the
running version of the plugin, so a deleted version folder cannot strand an
entry. 'py -3' is the Windows Python launcher. On macOS and Linux replace
"py" and the "-3" argument with "python3" and drop the "-3". There is no
per-platform branch available in this format, so the choice is documented
rather than solved.
WHAT IS REGISTERED (twelve entries). The gates are the concept gate, the
architecture guard and the plain-language guard. As of operator decision 8 of
2026-10-09 this plugin also registers BOTH database guards itself:
db-destructive-guard.py on the edit group, Bash and PowerShell, and
db-research-readonly-guard.py on Bash and PowerShell (it left the edit group).
The four post-edit trackers run inside ONE asynchronous dispatcher,
post-edit-dispatcher.py, so an edit starts one process instead of four.
BLAST RADIUS: these are enforcement gates, not suggestions. Installing this
plugin turns them on. concept-gate blocks Edit/Write on non-trivial files until
an approved concept contract exists, and the database guards fail CLOSED, which
means every database is treated as protected when the project's rules file is
absent, unreadable or empty, or when CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is not set. The guards
read <project>/.claude/hooks/db-destructive-guard.rules.json and never the
template that ships beside them (that template names only the fictional
databases AcmeApp and AcmeApp_Testing). The advisory hooks read their rules
project-first too, and fall back to the shipped template. README.md lists the
per-hook environment-variable kill switches.
